Later on, Writ Petition (L) No.
23609 of 2024 was de-
tagged and is listed before a co-ordinate Bench on 11th August 2025.

WRIT PETITION (L) NO. 9223 OF 2025 AND WRIT PETITION (L) NO. 9252 OF 2025:
2.

Writ Petition (L) No. 9223 of 2025 and Writ Petition (L) No. 9252 of 2025 have been assigned to a Bench presided over by one of us (Coram: Shree Chandrashekhar J.) by an order passed by Hon'ble the Chief Justice on administrative side on 6th August 2025.

Stating that there was extreme urgency and these writ petitions are required to be heard immediately, a praecipe dated 7 th August 2025 was moved by Ms Surnedra J. Farro, the learned counsel for the petitioners in these writ petitions.

4. These writ petitions were directed to be listed today at the top of the board and we have heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner- NGO, namely, Adivas Mumbaikar Shetkari Samiti &
Nyas (NGO).

sentences.text: The petitioner-NGO has pleaded that it is the authorized Agent of 114 persons who are slum dwellers and it is the Authority- holder on their behalf.

The petitioner- NGO seeks to refer to 22 Statutes and Government Circulars including the Maharashtra Slum Areas (Improvement,
Clearance and Redevelopment) Act, 1971, Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966,
Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act, 1888, Land Acquisition Act, 1894, Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, Land Acquisition (Companies) Rules, 1963, Societies Registration Act, 1860 etc.

sentences.text: The petitioner- NGO also seeks to challenge the orders passed by this Court in Writ Petition No.1580 of 2017, Writ Petition No. 1036 of 2017, Writ Petition No. 3146 of 2024 and Writ Petition No. 10849 of 2024.
There are other diverse prayers made in these writ petitions.

In sum and substance, the learned counsel for the petitioner- NGO submits that a fraud was played upon by the Developer, namely, Arihant Constructions Company and demolitions are being carried out by virtue of illegal notices issued by the Slum Rehabilitation Authority-respondent no.5.

However, the learned counsel for the petitioners is not able to demonstrate how the notices issued by the R.V.Patil 4/4 918 WP(L).9223.2025.odt Slum Rehabilitation Authority - respondent no. 5 can be labeled as illegal.
There are statutory regimes under which the aggrieved party can seek redressal of his grievance.
This writ petition is also not maintainable to the extent that it seeks to challenge the orders passed by the writ Court which have become final.
6. In the aforementioned factual background, we are not inclined to call upon the respondents to file their reply affidavits.

There is another reason for doing so and that is after arguing for some time the learned counsel for the petitioner-NGO seeks permission to withdraw these writ petitions with liberty to the petitioner- NGO to take up its grievances before the appropriate Authority and to explore remedy as available to it in law.
7. Writ Petition (L) No. 9223 of 2025 and Writ Petition (L) No. 9252 of 2025 are dismissed as withdrawn.
